# UX guidelines catalog — universal a11y/UX pass

A thin guide to `agent/references/data/ux-guidelines.csv` — a catalogue
of **99 universal interaction / accessibility / performance rules**
used as a **secondary** review pass after the skill's own
register-aware self-checks.

This file is small on purpose: it tells you **when to read the CSV**,
**how to filter it**, and **what to do with violations**. The data
itself stays out of context until you actually need it.

---

## Why this exists

Our own self-checks (in
`agent/skills/digital-product-poc/references/pitch-concept-site-21st.md
§ Self-check` and `agent/skills/deck-design-corporate/references/verification.md`)
are **opinionated** — they enforce AIMS, the creative ↔ technological
register split, the anti-AI-signal rules, the IA whitelist/blacklist.

They do NOT cover the vendor-neutral fundamentals: 4.5:1 contrast,
44×44 touch targets, focus rings on keyboard interactions, form
labels (not just placeholders), `prefers-reduced-motion`, etc. A
deck or POC can pass all our opinion-checks and still fail basic
a11y.

This catalogue is that floor.

---

## When to consult

**Read the CSV** (don't load it in advance — progressive disclosure):

1. **digital-product-poc Self-check phase** (always, when the
   output contains any interactive UI — buttons, forms, links,
   nav). Filter by current `register` and
   `severity ∈ {error, warning}`.
2. **deck Self-check phase** — only when the deck contains
   an interactive UI mockup (form, input, button beyond a static
   CTA). Filter to `severity == error` and `register_tag ==
universal`. Decks are mostly static; full UX-pass is overkill.

**Skip entirely** in:

- orchestrator (it doesn't evaluate UI quality)
- review-presentation (human-review surface)
- brand-overlay / figma-conditional (separate axes)

---

## How to filter

The CSV has 11 columns:

| Column              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `No`                | Rule id (1–99)                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Category`          | Navigation / Animation / Layout / Touch / Interaction / Accessibility / Performance / Forms / Responsive / Typography / Feedback / Content / Onboarding / Search / Data Entry / AI Interaction / Spatial UI / Sustainability |
| `Issue`             | Short rule name                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Platform`          | `Web` / `Mobile` / `All` / `VisionOS`                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Description`       | One-line explanation                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Do`                | Recommended approach                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Don't`             | Anti-pattern                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Code Example Good` | Tailwind / CSS / JSX snippet                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Code Example Bad`  | Tailwind / CSS / JSX snippet                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Severity`          | `High` (error-level) / `Medium` (warning-level) / `Low` (info)                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Register Tag`      | `universal` (95 rules) / `technological_only` (4 rules: bulk-actions, AI disclaimer, AI streaming, AI feedback-loop) / `creative_only` (currently zero)                                                                      |

### Filter patterns

**digital-product-poc, register: creative, web output:**

```bash
awk -F, 'NR > 1 \
         && ($10 == "High" || $10 == "Medium") \
         && ($4 == "Web" || $4 == "All") \
         && ($11 == "universal" || $11 == "creative_only")' \
    agent/references/data/ux-guidelines.csv
```

**digital-product-poc, register: technological, web output:**

```bash
awk -F, 'NR > 1 \
         && ($10 == "High" || $10 == "Medium") \
         && ($4 == "Web" || $4 == "All") \
         && ($11 == "universal" || $11 == "technological_only")' \
    agent/references/data/ux-guidelines.csv
```

**deck, interactive mockup present, error-level only:**

```bash
awk -F, 'NR > 1 \
         && $10 == "High" \
         && ($4 == "Web" || $4 == "All") \
         && $11 == "universal"' \
    agent/references/data/ux-guidelines.csv
```

The CSV is small (~16 KB, 99 rows) — loading it directly with
`Read` is also fine. Use `awk` / `grep` when you want to keep
context tight.

---

## What to do with violations

Per the receiving skill's self-check section:

- **`Severity: High`** → escalate
  `ux_rule_violation: <No>: <Issue>: <section>: <fix-hint-from-Do>`
  in the output envelope's `escalation_flags`. **Blocks ship.**
- **`Severity: Medium`** → log to `review_notes[]` with the same
  shape. Does not block ship; surfaces in human-review.
- **`Severity: Low`** → skip during automated pass; humans can
  consult the catalog manually if they want to.

When fixing a violation, use the rule's `Code Example Good` as the
starting template — it's already Tailwind-flavoured so it merges
into our shadcn-based output cleanly.

## Identity preservation

This catalog is **additive**, never authoritative:

- It does NOT override our IA blacklist (no leaderboard /
  testimonial-card-grid / feature-grid-with-icons in `register:
creative`). If a rule from the catalog would lead us toward a
  blacklisted pattern (none currently does), the IA blacklist
  wins.
- It does NOT override Rule 9 ("nothing sits above a heading") —
  that's our anti-AI-signal rule, stronger than any standard a11y
  pattern.
- It does NOT touch the kit (`kit-corporate/shared/tokens.css`,
  `components.css`, `layouts.css`) or composition rules — its
  recommendations are CSS-property-level (contrast ratios,
  durations, viewport units), not layout-grammar level.

If a rule conflicts with a kit token or composition rule, **kit
wins**. The catalog is fundamentals; the kit and AIMS are taste.

**Local modifications:**

- Added column `Register Tag` (`universal` /
  `technological_only` / `creative_only`) so our register-aware
  self-checks can filter rules by current register.
- 95 rules marked `universal`. 4 rules marked
  `technological_only`: 91 (Bulk Actions), 92 (AI Disclaimer), 93
  (AI Streaming), 98 (AI Feedback Loop) — these fundamentally
  apply only to SaaS/B2B contexts; surfacing them on a concert /
  editorial site as warnings would be noise.
- Zero `creative_only` rules currently. The catalog's data is
  vendor-neutral enough that nearly everything applies regardless
  of register.

No other modifications. The raw rule text, code examples, and
severity grades are unchanged.
